statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r equals the number of closed islands of grid, defined as follows. A cell is a pair (i,j) with 0 <= i < R and 0 <= j < C; it is land if grid[i][j] = 0 and water if grid[i][j] = 1. Two cells (i,j) and (i',j') are 4-adjacent if |i-i'| + |j-j'| = 1. A set S of cells is 4-connected if for every a,b in S there is a finite sequence a = c_0, c_1, ..., c_k = b of cells in S such that c_t and c_{t+1} are 4-adjacent for every 0 <= t < k (and k = 0 when a = b). A land island is a maximal 4-connected set of land cells: S is a land island if S is a nonempty 4-connected set of land cells and no land cell outside S is 4-adjacent to any cell in S. A cell (i,j) is interior if 1 <= i <= R-2 and 1 <= j <= C-2; otherwise it lies on the grid boundary (i=0 or i=R-1 or j=0 or j=C-1). A land island is closed if every cell in it is interior. Then r is the number of closed islands.
preconditions: Let R = len(grid) and C = len(grid[0]). Assume 1 <= R <= 100, 1 <= C <= 100, len(grid[i]) = C for every 0 <= i < R, and grid[i][j] ∈ {0,1} for every 0 <= i < R and 0 <= j < C.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r <= I, where I is defined by I = 0 if R < 2 or C < 2, and I = (R-2)*(C-2) otherwise.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, r = 0 if and only if every land cell is connected to some boundary cell by a path of land cells; that is, for every land cell (i,j) there exists a sequence (i_0,j_0), ..., (i_k,j_k) of land cells with (i_0,j_0)=(i,j), each consecutive pair 4-adjacent, and the last cell (i_k,j_k) satisfying i_k=0 or i_k=R-1 or j_k=0 or j_k=C-1.

statement: Whenever the function returns r, if there is exactly one cell (i0,j0) with grid[i0][j0] = 0, and 1 <= i0 <= R-2 and 1 <= j0 <= C-2, then r = 1.

Whenever the function returns r on grid, r equals the number of closed islands of grid^T, where closed islands of grid^T are defined by the same definition as in spec_1 with grid^T in place of grid.
